title: Keep undefined percent-only method comparisons unresolved
prompt:
Prevent an unmeasurable sole acceptance criterion from producing acceptable in lib/ohworks-method-comparison.ts. Lines 341-342 set percentBias to null when the mean reference is zero. Lines 368-381 then skip the percentage check and retain acceptable. Verified reproduction: reference values -10 and 10, candidate values 90 and 110, matching mg/dL units, minPairs 2, loaMultiplier 1.96, and allowableBias {maxMeanDifference:null,maxPercentBias:5} returns acceptable despite a mean difference of 100 and no evaluable declared criterion. The demo renders the decision through lib/ohworks-demo-method-performance-view.ts:228-242, which already handles MethodComparisonError as unresolved.

When percent bias is the sole declared acceptance axis and the reference mean is zero, throw MethodComparisonError with a new percent-bias-unavailable code and clear explanation. Keep the documented null statistic and current behavior when an absolute mean-difference limit is also declared or is the sole criterion. Preserve normal percentage comparisons, calculations, and existing error precedence. Do not modify the view or add policy for other numerical cases.

Add tests/ohworks/method-comparison-unavailable-bias.test.ts reproducing the false acceptance, an identical zero-mean pair set with the same unavailable sole criterion, a zero-mean absolute-limit control, and a nonzero-mean percentage control. Assert the typed error code and explanation. Run node --import tsx --test tests/ohworks/method-comparison-unavailable-bias.test.ts tests/ohworks/method-comparison.test.ts tests/ohworks/demo-method-performance-view.test.ts. Use synthetic data; work on the assigned branch you are on. Edit only the named production file and new test. No credentials, deploys, sends, payments, migrations, workflows, package.json, auth changes, commits, or pushes.
